$comment: Source of truth for the NFC.cool design system.
src/tokens.css, src/brands/*.css and src/email.css are GENERATED from this file by build/emit-css.mjs.
defaultBrand names the brand that also answers on :root, feeds src/email.css and fills the dist/ bundles.
Every value here is derived from nfc-cool-website's own CSS, or computed fresh
against its palette. Nothing is imported from any other project.

breakpoints.$comment: A var() cannot appear in a media condition, so these are constants enforced by test/guards.test.mjs. nfc.cool's seven literal breakpoints (1199/900/768/760/600/540/480) fold into these four: 760->md, 540->sm, 480->sm, 1199->xl.

space.$comment: 4px grid. Keeps 1.25rem (space-5) because 20px is nfc.cool's signature grid gap and dropping it would re-space every card grid on the site.

section.$comment: The three clamp() rhythms already present in landing.css / marketing.css / features.css, named.

text.$comment: Collapses ~14 unique clamp() expressions in the shipped CSS into one ladder.
text.title: clamp(1.75rem, 3.5vw, 2.5rem)
text.heading: clamp(1.625rem, 3vw, 2.25rem)

tracking.$comment: The system's real typographic signature: negative on display sizes, positive on uppercase micro-labels. Reset to normal for Arabic, which is a connected script.
tracking.heading: -0.015em
tracking.label: 0.04em

radius.$comment: nfc.cool's existing six, unchanged. 'base' and 'lg' are the two SiteKit emits from theme.yaml; the rest come from theme.css.

elevation.$comment: Six ad-hoc shadows in the shipped CSS become four steps. These reference brand-layer shadow colors, resolved at use time.

nav.$comment: Navigation geometry. One component, two modes: data-nav=bar lays the same parts along the inline axis, data-nav=side along the block axis. The rail width is a touch target plus the icon, not a shrunken sidebar; the stacked rail is wide enough for a two-line label under it.

motion.$comment: Deliberately tiny: one duration, one gesture. No scroll animation, no reveal-on-scroll. Lift distances are tokenised so the three tiers stay distinguishable.

font.heading: "Titillium Web", -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", sans-serif
font.mono: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, "SF Mono", Menlo, Consolas, "Liberation Mono", monospace

light.$accent-note: #FFC700 is the Secondary Logo SVG's value in Brand Manual V1, chosen as authoritative over the #FFC709 the website shipped. Never text on a light surface: it measures 1.45:1. The wordmark tail is the one exception, permitted as a logotype under WCAG 1.4.3.
light.$brand-blue-note: FIXED. These are the iOS app's appThemeGradient, dark at the top and light at the bottom, so the web band matches what the product actually renders. Chosen over NFC_Gradient.png (same-family colours, mirrored) and over the manual's Dark/Light Blue swatches, which the dashboard and email templates ramp between but which are not the brand gradient. Not a styling choice: do not darken them for contrast. White clears AA at the top and holds above the large-text floor at the bottom; --on-brand-text-shadow carries body copy over the lower half, and the two travel together.
light.$link-note: The interactive colours ARE the two gradient stops, not tints derived from them. --color-link is the light stop, used where 3:1 is the bar (borders, chevrons, icons, hover fills). --color-link-text is the dark stop at 5.38:1 on the page, used for text.
light.$primary-note: The filled primary is the gradient's light stop with a WHITE label. That pairing measures 3.48:1, below the 4.5 a 15px label needs, and is a deliberate brand decision recorded as an exception in test/contrast.test.mjs rather than silently shipped. Hover DARKENS to #0F76CA, which lifts the label to 4.70:1, so the state a person is actively pointing at is the compliant one. If the exception is ever revisited, #0F78CE is the nearest shade of the same blue where white clears 4.5 at rest.

dark.$glow-note: In the dark theme the gradient collapses to the page background plus a faint glow in the brand accent; the light theme has no glow. The glow lives here, not in the generator, so a second brand glows in its own accent.
